title: Compat API stats with one-shot=true returns an erratic cpu_stats.cpu
body:
### Issue Description

For a container with a constant load `GET /containers/{id}/stats?stream=false&one-shot=true` (Docker-compat API) returns a `cpu_stats.cpu` that is 0 most of the time but sometimes a large positive number.

I'm not sure whether this field is meant to be reliable in one-shot mode, but at least one client (Pulse) trusts it when it is positive.

This all comes because I have Pulse and Arcane as podman manager and I see different CPU usages between tools (and then Pulse is the source for HomeAssistant's graphs)

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Run a container that stresses exactly one core:

```
podman run -d --name stress docker.io/library/alpine sh -c 'while :; do :; done'
```

2. Poll the endpoint once a second and look at `cpu_stats.cpu`:

```
for i in $(seq 150); do
  curl -s --unix-socket /run/user/$UID/podman/podman.sock \
    "http://d/containers/stress/stats?stream=false&one-shot=true" | jq .cpu_stats.cpu
  sleep 1
done
```

3. Optionally repeat with a second container limited to 0.5 CPU (`--cpus 0.5`).



### Describe the results you received

Over 150 seconds, with a container using exactly one core and another capped at half a core:

| Host | Container load | Samples with non-zero `cpu_stats.cpu` | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 vCPU VM | one core | 18 of 147 (12%) | 203 to 967 |
| 8 vCPU VM | half core | 13 of 147 (9%) | 181 to 811 |
| Raspberry Pi 3B+ (4 CPUs, arm64) | one core | 113 of 135 (84%) | 25 to 215 |
| Raspberry Pi 3B+ (4 CPUs, arm64) | half core | 73 of 135 (54%) | 1 to 215 |

The container's real usage is steady. The deltas of `cpu_stats.cpu_usage.total_usage` over time, the kernel's cgroup `cpu.stat` and `podman stats` all give 100% and 50% of one core.


### Describe the results you expected

In one-shot mode, `cpu_stats.cpu` should either be consistently unset/0, or a value that matches the real usage of the container, like `podman stats` reports.

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

No

### Additional environment details

- Debian 13 (trixie) VM on Proxmox, 8 vCPUs, amd64, Podman 5.4.2 from the Debian package, rootless, crun, cgroup v2, `podman.socket` as a systemd user service.
- Raspberry Pi 3B+ (4 CPUs, arm64), Debian 13, same Podman 5.4.2.


### Additional information

It happens only occasionally on the VM (about 10% of the samples) and much more often on the Pi (about 55 to 85%).

I have not tried the latest release at runtime (my package is Debian's 5.4.2), but looking around  v5.8.8 and v6.1.3 and the logic looks unchanged. In `pkg/api/handlers/compat/containers_stats.go` the handler calls `ctnr.GetContainerStats(nil)` and then `ctnr.GetContainerStats(stats)` right after in the same request, using the first sample as the previous one. In `libpod/stats_linux.go`, `calculateCPUPercent` computes `cpuDelta / (now - previousSystem) * 100`. In one-shot mode the two samples are only milliseconds apart, so the cgroup counter either has not advanced (0) or has jumped by a whole tick (several hundred percent). With `stream=true` the previous sample is a full interval old.

This looks related to #24730, where the same field is described as only being populated on the second run.

Suggested behaviour: in one-shot mode, don't report a `cpu` percentage (leave it unset/0 consistently), or calculate it against a sample that is at least some reasonable interval old.

comments.body:
Since i didn't realize how out of date the debian podman was, I installed 6.1.3 from `mgoltzsche/podman-static` on both hosts and the behaviour is the same.

Over 150 seconds, `cpu_stats.cpu` was non-zero in 16% (one core) and 10% (half core) of the samples on the 8 vCPU VM, with values between 239 and 821, and in 85% and 50% of the samples on the Raspberry Pi 3B+, with values between 6 and 187.

The compat stats handler calls `GetContainerStats(nil)` then immediately `GetContainerStats(stats)`, passing the first result as the previous sample. The `calculateCPUPercent` computes with only milliseconds between the two calls, the cgroup counter either hasn't advanced (0) or has jumped by a whole scheduler tick (hundreds of percent).

The fix zeros `cpu_stats.cpu` when `one-shot=true`. This is a Podman-specific extension field. Docker doesn't have it, and the [Docker API spec](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/api/types/container/stats.go#L217-L223) says `PreRead` and `PreCPUStats` are not propagated for one-shot. With samples only milliseconds apart there is no way to report a meaningful interval percentage without a background collector or a blocking delay, neither of which fits Podman's daemonless architecture.

Clients that need a CPU percentage should use `stream=true`, or `stream=false` without one-shot and compute deltas across their own polling interval using `cpu_stats.cpu_usage.total_usage` and `cpu_stats.system_cpu_usage`.

@hihry Could you please close PR [#29914](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/29914) and review my existing PR [#29599](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/29599) instead? Also, please focus on finishing your previous work first.
